_meta.description: The five defined events and the privacy rules for recording them. The client-side counter (assets/js/analytics.js) records first-party, cookieless events; the self-hosted collector (collector/app.py) is the optional endpoint. Events mirror the carried attribution model in the ledger.

events.name: page_view
events.definition: A page of this site was loaded by a visitor. Recorded client-side, first-party only.
events.privacy: No cookies; path and timestamp only; no IP, no user-agent stored.

events.name: product_link_click
events.definition: A visitor activated a Special Link (any anchor to an Amazon site, all marked rel=sponsored). Starts the attribution session as Amazon measures it.
events.where: analytics.js click listener on sponsored anchors
events.privacy: Records the destination path and timestamp only.

events.name: chooser_step
events.definition: A visitor answered a step of the three-question chooser on the comparison page.
events.privacy: Step index and chosen label; nothing else.

events.name: article_read
events.definition: A visitor scrolled a guide past the three-quarter mark of the article body.
events.where: analytics.js scroll listener on guide pages

events.name: guide_to_compare_click
events.definition: A visitor followed a guide's link to the comparison page - the site's core conversion path.
events.where: analytics.js click listener on data-cc=guide-to-compare anchors

privacy_commitments: No cookies, no fingerprinting, no cross-site identifiers, no IP addresses stored, no user-agent strings stored.
Aggregation first: counts accumulate in the visitor's browser (localStorage) and are the primary display; the collector receives anonymous event lines only if window.CC_COLLECT_URL is configured.
The click counter is a first-party measurement and is never presented as a reported order; orders enter the ledger only from authorised Associates Central reports (D-10).
Retention when the collector is hosted: event lines are kept 90 days by default, then rotated; the owner sets the final policy when choosing the host (Q-06).
